claim: Daily vitamin D supplementation of 800-1000 IU/day is consistently safe and recommended for correction of deficiency/insufficiency in adults
stance_target: 2000 IU/day Vitamin D3 softgel safety and efficacy
scope_conditions: Multiple RCTs; adults and elderly; primarily European/North American populations
quoted_support: The prevention and/or correction of vitamin D deficiency/insufficiency with 800–1000 IU/daily of vitamin D or 10 µg/day of calcifediol are safe. Because of their potential harm, larger doses given on the long term or in intermittent regimens should not be selected.
numbers: 800-1000 IU/day safe and effective for deficiency correction
4000 IU/day widely accepted upper safety limit

claim: Vitamin D3 supplementation combined with calcium reduces fracture risk: 6% reduction in any fracture and 16% reduction in hip fracture in meta-analysis of RCTs
stance_target: Vitamin D3 bone health efficacy claims
scope_conditions: Meta-analysis of six RCTs, predominantly using 800 IU/day vitamin D
quoted_support: In the most recent meta-analysis, the association vitamin D and calcium was associated with a 6 and 16% reduction of any fracture and hip fracture, respectively. In this analysis, five out of six included randomized controlled trials were using 800 IU/day.
entities: Yao P et al. JAMA Netw Open 2019

claim: High-dose vitamin D (4000-10,000 IU/day) may paradoxically harm bone density: a 3-year RCT found volumetric BMD declined -2.4% and -3.5% at 4000 and 10,000 IU/day vs -1.2% at 400 IU/day
stance_target: High-dose vitamin D superiority for bone health
scope_conditions: RCT, 311 healthy vitamin D-replete 62-year-old subjects, 3 years
quoted_support: At the end of 3 years, changes in distal radius volumetric BMD, as assessed by high resolution peripheral QCT, were − 1.2, − 2.4 and − 3.5% in the 400, 4000 and 10,000 IU/day groups, respectively. The values in the two latter groups were significantly lower than in the 400 IU group.

claim: Vitamin D3 (cholecalciferol) supplementation reduces all-cause mortality, while D2 and active vitamin D metabolites do not show the same benefit
stance_target: D3 form superiority over D2 in supplements
scope_conditions: Systematic review and meta-analysis of observational cohort and RCT data; adult populations
quoted_support: Vitamin D3, but not vitamin D2 nor vitamin D active metabolites supplementation was associated with a lower mortality. Vitamin D with calcium reduced mortality by 6% in a patient level pooled analysis of 70,528 patients from 8 vitamin trials.

claim: Daily doses of 800-1000 IU vitamin D consistently demonstrate beneficial effects on muscle strength and balance in older adults; higher doses do not show additional muscle benefit
stance_target: Vitamin D3 muscle function efficacy at 2000 IU/day
scope_conditions: Systematic review and meta-analysis, older adults, 2011; dose-dependent analysis
quoted_support: In a systematic review and meta-analysis published in 2011, the conclusion was that daily doses of 800 to 1000 IU consistently demonstrated beneficial effects on muscle strength and balance.
numbers: 1000 IU/day increased lower limb muscle strength
2800 IU/day reduced grip strength −9% and knee flexion −13% in some trials

claim: The upper safety limit of 4000 IU/day for vitamin D may be too high for elderly women with fall history; medium doses of 1600-3200 IU/day reduce falls while 4000-4800 IU/day do not show benefit over placebo
stance_target: 2000 IU/day Vitamin D3 supplementation fall prevention safety
scope_conditions: RCT in elderly women (66 years, 25OHD <50 nmol/L), 12 months
quoted_support: There was a significant decrease in falls with medium doses of 1600, 2400 and 3200 IU/day. In contrast, with the high doses of 4,000 and 4800 IU/day, fall rates were as high as in the placebo group and significantly higher than with the medium doses.
entities: Smith LM, Gallagher JC. J Steroid Biochem Mol Biol 2017

claim: A 3-year RCT found hypercalcemia occurred in 3% at 4000 IU/day and 9% at 10,000 IU/day versus 0% at 400 IU/day in healthy 62-year-old adults
scope_conditions: RCT, 373 healthy 62-year-old subjects, 3 years, vitamin D-replete at baseline
quoted_support: Hypercalcemia (total serum calcium > 2.55 mmol/l) occurred in 0, 3 and 9% in the 400, 4000 and 10,000 IU/day groups, respectively. A 24-h urinary excretion higher than 7.5 mmol/day, which defined hypercalciuria, was detected in 17, 22 and 31% of the corresponding groups.

claim: Vitamin D supplementation is effective for bone health primarily in subjects who have baseline 25OHD deficiency (below 50 nmol/L); no BMD benefit shown in vitamin D-replete subjects
stance_target: Vitamin D3 bone health claims for general supplementation
scope_conditions: VITAL study (2000 IU/day, 2 years, subjects with normal vitamin D status mean 25OHD 77 nmol/L) and other RCTs
quoted_support: In another trial conducted in subjects with a normal vitamin D status (mean baseline 25OHD: 77 nmol/l), vitamin D supplements of 2000 IU/day of cholecalciferol did not influence areal BMD at the spine, hip or whole body level over 2 years (VITAL study).
numbers: 2000 IU/day no BMD effect in replete subjects
entities: LeBoff MS et al. J Bone Miner Res 2020
